title: Fail loudly when systemd-resolved will not start after networkd retirement
head: 02d1e01ee9e7
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Historical migration now requires resolved even when a different DNS provider works
leads.consequence: On an existing non-live host with a regular /etc/resolv.conf or a symlink to a third-party resolver, systemd-resolved may be deliberately masked. The changed unconditional enable --now then fails after the migration has disabled networkd; bash -e makes the migration fail, omarchy-migrate does not touch the per-user marker or run later migrations, and each update repeats the failed attempt even though the host's independent DNS may be healthy. Before this PR, the resolved restart was allowed to fail. This regression precedes the final fix commit (first two commits). Failing with a stub link is deliberate; failing for nonstub hosts is the unnecessary part.

leads.summary: Recovery excludes systemd's supported static 127.0.0.53 stub link
leads.consequence: An existing installation that links /etc/resolv.conf to /usr/lib/systemd/resolv.conf (or an equivalent relative text) has 127.0.0.53 as its only DNS server. When resolved is inactive, this recovery's string comparison returns false, exits 0 without enabling the service, and omarchy-migrate writes the marker. The next run skips it; DNS for clients using resolv.conf stays broken until manual repair. The Quattro upgrade writer and systemd boot default use the now-accepted relative dynamic stub, so the original F1 is fixed for them; this is a distinct supported static mode.

leads.summary: Missing resolv.conf is treated as permanently safe despite boot-time stub creation
leads.consequence: For an existing host where /etc/resolv.conf is absent during the update and resolved is masked (or disabled and not activated by another path), the migration explicitly exits successfully without checking the unit and receives a completion marker. On the next boot, systemd's L! tmpfiles rule creates ../run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf at /etc/resolv.conf if missing. Unless the administrator overrides that vendor tmpfiles rule or starts resolved separately, this leaves stub DNS pointed at an inactive service without a pending recovery; future migration runs skip it. This is a conditional lifecycle gap, not a claim that normal freshly installed machines lack the service (the Omarchy installer enables it).

leads.summary: Focused test does not exercise other-link rejection, privilege boundary, or historical call sites
leads.consequence: The other-link fixture is defined but never called. A plausible classifier mutant that treats every nonempty symlink as the resolved stub passes all seven head tests, yet would try to enable resolved on an administrator's unrelated resolver. The fake systemctl also succeeds without sudo, so a mutant that removes as_root passes despite non-root installations where direct enable is denied. The historical assertions are grep-only; omitting both ensure_systemd_resolved calls while leaving the unused function intact also passes, even though start failures would once again be swallowed. Add a negative other-link run, a sudo stub that records or enforces elevation, and a failed-start runtime exercise of the historical migration. None of these mutants describes the actual current production code; the actual relative-link test does fail against the previous revision.

limits: No real service/systemd changes or host /etc/resolv.conf reads were made; runs use stub commands and sandbox-private synthetic resolv.conf symlinks.

The inspected Arch systemd PKGBUILD at query time reports v262; an installed Omarchy system's exact systemd version is not asserted. The documented static stub and tmpfiles default are present at v262.

No overlapping open PR modifies any of the three changed files in this PR among the related reviewed PRs; full cross-PR merged test runs were not performed. The open PR #13362 is reported by GitHub as CONFLICTING for the branch, for changes outside this PR's three changed files; this hunt makes no mergeability claim for #12909.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12909#issuecomment-5787201764) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12909#issuecomment-5841738187), checked at head `02d1e01e`.

**Verified:** The relative-link finding is resolved, and the earlier note about the historical migration still holds. One new, narrow issue in the historical migration's new `ensure_systemd_resolved` is described below. It dates from the first commit, not from the latest fix.

| Earlier finding | Status at `02d1e01e` |
|---|---|
| Recovery skips the upgrade's relative stub link | **Resolved** |
| Historical migration propagates a failed resolved start | **Still holds** (file unchanged) |

**Verified:** [`uses_stub_resolv`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/02d1e01ee9e7fc8e6021d7c91e2d8f2c17812ef2/migrations/1790048120.sh#L14-L22) now accepts both `/run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf` and `../run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf`. The relative form is the one written by `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` and by systemd's own tmpfiles default. Through the real migration runner, with stubbed service commands, a relative link with an inactive resolved gives:

| Revision | Service calls | Exit | Marker | Final state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1aee0b17` (earlier) | none | 0 | written | inactive |
| `02d1e01e` | `enable --now` | 0 | written | active |
| `02d1e01e`, start fails or unit masked | `enable --now` | 1 | not written | inactive |

The new relative-link test case fails against the `1aee0b17` recovery migration, so it guards the fix.

### Historical migration now fails for accounts that cannot start resolved, even where it is not needed

[`ensure_systemd_resolved`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/02d1e01ee9e7fc8e6021d7c91e2d8f2c17812ef2/migrations/1782002156.sh#L14-L20) always runs `systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service` through `as_root` (so through `sudo` for a normal user) and then requires `is-active`. It does not first check whether resolved is already active, and it does not check whether `/etc/resolv.conf` uses the stub. The merge-base's earlier `restart` call swallowed any failure.

Isolated runs of the non-live branch through the migration runner, with stubbed `sudo` and `systemctl`:

| Host state | Head | Merge-base `7b336b1b` |
|---|---|---|
| resolved active, account without sudo rights | exit 1, no marker | exit 0, marker |
| non-stub `/etc/resolv.conf`, resolved masked | exit 1, no marker | exit 0, marker |
| resolved active, sudo allowed | exit 0, marker | exit 0, marker |

**Impact:** A failed migration stops that account's migration queue, so every later migration stays pending. This path is reached by accounts that run this migration after the upgrade, for example another user on a machine upgraded from Omarchy 3, where the migration is still unstamped. For an account without sudo rights this happens even when resolved is healthy. `agents/skills/migrations.md` asks that a machine-wide repair already applied by one user be a no-op for the next. During the Quattro upgrade itself the stub link is always present, so failing there remains appropriate.

**Suggested change:** Return early from `ensure_systemd_resolved` when `systemctl is-active --quiet systemd-resolved.service` already succeeds, and fail only when `/etc/resolv.conf` points at the stub, as the recovery migration already does before calling `sudo`.

**Optional test improvement:** The test checks `1782002156.sh` only by text. Replacing both `ensure_systemd_resolved` call sites with `true` still passes all cases. Running the historical migration once with the failing `systemctl` stub and asserting a non-zero exit would cover the behaviour the test header describes. That run needs `/etc/systemd/network` pointed at the test directory, as `/etc/resolv.conf` already is, and a `NetworkManager` stub on PATH, because the migration moves stock networkd files and installs NetworkManager when it is missing.

**Documentation:** The PR description still names the recovery migration `1790044019`; the file is `1790048120.sh`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `02d1e01e`, compared with the earlier head `1aee0b17` and the merge-base `7b336b1b`. Source inspection plus isolated runs of the migrations through the real runner, with stubbed `sudo` and service commands. No live systemd, DNS, NetworkManager or full upgrade run. The Quattro upgrade's final package sync still runs before migrations, so these checks do not cover recovery from DNS failures before migrations are reached. Which accounts reach the non-live branch comes from reading the source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
